raw_response:
As of **April 18, 2026**, in Quzhou the **winter wheat is already in the field**, cotton planting is starting, and summer maize will go in right after wheat harvest in June. I’ll manage it the way I usually do, not chasing fancy numbers. I’m 65 and there’s only one person at home, so I can’t spread myself too thin. I’ll keep the **wheat-maize on 10 mu**, because that is steady money and grain in hand, and I’ll put **8.8 mu into cotton** since I’ve grown it many years and know how to handle it. I mainly follow what has worked on my land and what the better farmers nearby do. Wheat I won’t push too hard now, just one more fertilizer pass if the leaves look light, and water when it really needs it. After wheat comes off in early June, I’ll plant maize quickly, with simple tillage so I don’t miss the window. Cotton takes more hand work, so I won’t put too much land there, but I’ll still grow it because if grain price is weak, cotton can help make up some cash. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I only water at the key times.
